description: A conditional whose branches cannot be brought together is refused at COMPILE time, and live words it by naming the offending OPERAND and the type the FIRST branch expects - so the sentence TURNS AROUND with the branches. ONE pair is worded differently and does NOT turn around: a TIME beside a TIMESTAMP reads 'incompatible types: [TIME(9)] and [TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9)]' with the TIME first however it was written, while a TIME beside a DATE is not that case and takes the ordinary sentence. What CONVERTS is as much the point as what does not: a VARIANT absorbs every scalar but a BINARY, a string meets a number, a temporal or a boolean, and a number meets a boolean - those must keep running, and a conversion that can only fail at ROW time is still accepted here. The SCALAR families are the whole scope; live is just as strict about OBJECT and ARRAY beside a scalar, but that half is measured and left to its own task. The other conditionals - IFF, CASE, NVL, GREATEST, LEAST - answer the same way. Converted 1:1 from query/IncompatibleBranchTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ic (i INT, v VARCHAR(5), d DATE, tm TIME, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ, bo BOOLEAN, bn BINARY(5), va VARIANT, ob OBJECT, ar ARRAY, tl TIMESTAMP_LTZ, vn VARCHAR(5))
INSERT INTO ic SELECT 1, 'ab', '2020-01-01', '10:00:00', '2020-01-01 10:00:00', TRUE, TO_BINARY('AB'), TO_VARIANT(1), OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1), ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(1, 2), '2020-01-01 10:00:00', '123'
